page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.12xlarge is a general-purpose, burstable compute instance driven by the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor capable of frequencies up to 3.9 GHz, providing 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache, complemented by vector extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX instructions. Memory capacity is 192.0 GB of DDR5 RAM rated at 7 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, relying solely on network-attached options alongside an 11 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong general performance across integer, instruction-level, and memory-bound tasks. The instance placed in the top 25% for Geekbench single-core (2,145.0) and multi-core (19,542.0) metrics, supported by top-tier image processing (19,148.0) and strong Clang software compilation (52,977.0). Memory subsystem throughput scored in the top 25% for cached read bandwidth (3,834.86 GB/sec) and uncached large-block reads (191.08 GB/sec), while large-block write operations (77.41 GB/sec) registered in the average tier. PassMark results reflect high compute and database throughput, with an overall CPU score of 69,378.72 and strong database operation throughput at 23,134.23.

The CPU's advanced instruction support, including AMX, delivers notable acceleration for CPU-based machine learning inference. For small (135M) language models, text generation reached top-tier speeds of 340.25 tokens per second with prompt processing at 2,994.41 tokens per second. Inference performance for medium (7B) and large (70B) parameter models remains within the strong tier, achieving 28.34 tokens per second and 3.08 tokens per second in text generation, respectively.

Because the m8i-flex tier operates on burstable CPU allocation without bundled local storage, it provides resource density cost efficiencies for variable workloads over dedicated sustained-compute nodes. Workload profiles that align best with the m8i-flex.12xlarge include distributed enterprise databases, Redis caching clusters (measuring 87.32 million operations per second), static web serving fleets, parallel CI/CD builds, and CPU-driven machine learning inference pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 48 burstable vCPUs (24 physical cores) on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, paired with 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory. Utilizing the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance includes 480 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX acceleration, while omitting integrated GPUs and local disk storage in favor of an 11 Gbps baseline network link. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top 25% for Geekbench compute, Clang software building, cached memory reads, and Redis operations reaching 87.32 million ops/sec. CPU-based machine learning inference achieves top-tier results on smaller models alongside strong performance across 7B and 70B parameter targets. The platform provides a balanced resource structure optimal for caching layers, enterprise web applications, software compilation pipelines, and transactional database tasks.
